objective: Make post cards appear complete in one go: each card waits behind a stable skeleton until its images are decoded (bounded by a timeout and a failure fallback), images sit in a fixed 4:3 frame so nothing shifts, only the visible cards plus a small window ahead are prepared, a refetch keeps the cards already shown, and the bundle is split by route so the main chunk is under Vite's 500 kB warning.
acceptance_criteria: A post card in the feed, search results, a profile's posts and a thread (root and replies) renders the existing Skeleton post variant, aria-hidden and the same height class for every card, until it is ready, then the whole card at once: author, text, data-link preview (FRONTEND-014's components) and images appear in the same render, never piecemeal.

A card is ready when every image it shows (its own, and a reposted or quoted original's) has loaded and HTMLImageElement.decode() has resolved or rejected; a card with no images is ready at once; readiness is computed by one hook (e.g. features/feed/useCardReady.ts) that every list uses.

Bounded failure: an image that errors, has a null s3_key_public, or has not decoded within 4000 ms (one named constant) no longer holds the card: the card is revealed with that image's frame showing a neutral 'Image unavailable' line in the same reserved space; no card stays a skeleton longer than the timeout, pinned with fake timers.

Every post image sits in a fixed 4:3 frame (aspect-ratio: 4 / 3, object-fit: contain, the letterbox a surface token), so the skeleton, the loaded image and the failure line occupy the same box; the skeleton post variant reserves that frame when the card has media (a skeleton prop, not a second variant).

Only the cards in view plus a window ahead (an IntersectionObserver rootMargin of one viewport height below, one named constant) start loading their images; a card further down stays a skeleton until it enters that window; jsdom tests stub IntersectionObserver.

A refetch (invalidate after a like, reply, repost or delete; a window refocus) keeps every card already revealed on screen with its content, and never returns it to a skeleton; only a post whose images changed is prepared again. The previous page of results stays visible while the next page of a Load more is prepared.

Revealing has no animation (FrontendUI/components.md: no shimmer, nothing to switch off for reduced motion) and no keyframes at-rule (styles/base.test.ts); the feed region is aria-busy only while its first visible cards are being prepared.

routes.tsx loads the stats, games, players, compose, notifications, profile and auth pages with React.lazy behind one Suspense fallback (StatusLine); the feed, the thread modal and the app shell stay in the main chunk; `npm run build` prints no chunk-size warning (every chunk under 500 kB).

The modal flow keeps working with lazy pages: FRONTEND-014's detail-flow and modal-flow tests pass, the same dialog element persists, and a direct load of /games/<id> and /players/<id> is still the full page.

Every existing frontend test passes; typecheck, lint and build pass; 0x08-frontend.md records the readiness rule, the timeout, the window, the frame and the lazy routes (FrontendUI/components.md rows go in a Director PR: no unit role may write FrontendUI/).

Browser rows (vite preview against backend-dev, seeded posts with and without images and data links, light and dark, 360 and 1280 wide, Chromium DevTools network throttled to Slow 4G for the slow row): the feed shows skeletons then whole cards with no partial card; a slow image keeps its card a skeleton then reveals within 4 s with the image or the fallback line; an image URL that 404s reveals with 'Image unavailable'; Cumulative Layout Shift for the first screen under 0.1 (Performance panel or a PerformanceObserver layout-shift sum); liking a post does not flash any card back to a skeleton; the network panel shows route chunks loading on first visit to /stats and /compose.
